page: Amazon Web Services x2gd.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. The host is powered by an AWS Graviton2 processor using 64 physical ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz with dedicated single-threaded execution per core. It is configured with 1024 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding a 16:1 memory-to-core ratio of 16 GB RAM per core. The server includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps, with zero GPUs present.

Benchmark data demonstrates strong parallel throughput and caching performance. The server scores in the top 25% for multi-core stress-ng tests at 97,224.74 and achieves 3,794.5 GB/sec in cached small-block memory reads. It delivers exceptional Redis SET throughput at 74.05 million operations per second and high static web serving throughput of 45.92 GB/sec. In contrast, single-thread performance is limited, with weak single-core Geekbench scores of 982.0 and lower single-threaded compression speeds, reflecting the conservative 2.5 GHz base frequency and absence of x86 vector extensions.

Without hypervisor overhead or shared virtualization resources, the x2gd.metal offers exceptional memory density and hardware access for applications requiring extensive in-memory structures. It provides substantial cost efficiency per gigabyte of memory compared to traditional x86 alternatives, though users must consider the tradeoff of modest single-threaded compute and slow LLM token generation rates. The instance is optimally suited for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large-scale Redis clusters, electronic design automation, and high-throughput web serving pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services x2gd.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server offering 64 physical cores on an arm64 AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Designed without hypervisor overhead, it pairs 1024 GB of DDR4 memory (16 GB per core) with 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 25 Gbps network bandwidth. Benchmark profiles highlight strong multi-core processing, exceptional cached memory read throughput of 3794.5 GB/sec, and 74.05 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside robust static web serving. While single-thread execution and text generation benchmarks remain modest due to single-core frequency limits, its massive RAM density delivers strong cost-effective throughput for memory-heavy architectures. The server fits high-capacity in-memory databases, Redis caches, EDA simulation, and memory-intensive ETL pipelines.
